headline: GPU and memory-bounded methods speed up sequence alignment and variant calling
label: Gpu Accelerated Bioinformatics Tools
summary: Recent preprints and papers report GPU ports and memory-bounded algorithms cutting runtime for core genomics and sequence analysis tasks.
synthesis: The dominant thread is reducing computational cost of core sequence and genomics operations. Accelign ports dynamic-programming pairwise alignment (local, global, semi-global) to CUDA for DNA, RNA and protein sequences. cuBayes is a CUDA port of FreeBayes germline SNV calling that completes HG002/HG004 60x whole-genome analysis in about one minute on one GPU while maintaining algorithmic semantics. RAM-MSA addresses exact multiple sequence alignment with an anytime, memory-bounded path-finding approach supporting affine gap penalties. AutoZyme takes a different route, using an agentic framework to profile and iteratively optimize bioinformatics functions, reporting a median 8.52-fold runtime reduction. Codon optimization mapped onto Ising-model sampling for thermodynamic hardware, benchmarked against a genetic algorithm on the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, offers an energy-focused alternative. A separate fish protein identification study contributes a 2845-sequence dataset and benchmarks seven architectures.
